title: Machine Line

description: A factory street at sunset, and a line of machines that each do one thing to a number: times 3, plus 5. Build the line for 5 more than 3 times n and send a number through. Rebuild 3(x + 2) as a line that multiplies first, and find out when two lines always give the same output. Then run a line backward to find what went in, and mark the inputs that keep the output under 20. Plan a line, run it, and see what it really does. Every instruction is read aloud.
notes: Number Quest Unit 3 of the grades 6-8 street, The Machine Hall (grades 6-7): a Kit 2 game on Oomba3D 1.2.0 in the Toy Town theme 1.1.0 at sunset (ink outlines, gear button, graphics 'auto'), loaded with exactly kit2ImportMap() (tests/unit/machine-line.test.js checks the literal map). The street (ground, road, buildings, trees, street lights) is the theme's own pieces and the crates are its box; the loading dock (a short conveyor, one machine with a slow gear, a pallet) and the board's posts are the game's own simple meshes. The line of machines, the value boxes and the number line are drawn by the game on one board, shown as a page canvas over the 3D street (drawn at twice its size, outside the 3D haze and glow, so it stays crisp) where the 3D board stands in unseen: it pops in, shakes and sizes, and the page board follows it every frame. Three chapters of six rounds (lesson mode: chapter=build|same|undo and lock=1): Build the Line (3.1: write an expression as a line, work one out, read a line as an expression, a squaring machine, a story with a letter for a number), Same Output (3.2: always, sometimes or never the same; expand, combine like terms, factor, subtract a sum) and Run It Back (3.3: one-step and two-step equations solved by undoing, which line undoes another, an inequality as a ray on a number line). Plan first, then run: machine blocks put into slots, a stepper, a ray that can be dragged and flipped, or three tiles; a wrong plan is run and drawn as it really turns out (the output it gives beside the output wanted), with a spoken hint, and the round stays open. Two lines are compared as polynomials with whole-number arithmetic, never as text. No timer, no lives, no fail state, nothing typed, no balance, no reward currency. Read-aloud is on by default (BRB.speak, friendly voice): lines are written the way they are said. Machine blocks can be dragged onto a slot of the line (on a full line one takes that slot's place), dragged from slot to slot or off the board, or tapped. While a line is built the board writes what it makes (your line: 3(n + 5)); Build the Line opens with the order-of-operations rule, and the right-machines-wrong-order hints say why (without brackets, multiplying comes first; brackets come first). The first round's lines are asked for while the start card or menu shows (BRB.prefetchSpeech), and each round's closing line and the next question during the round, so the AI voice reads them from the first. Keys: 1 to 4 put a block in or out, Backspace takes the last out, arrows or + and - move the stepper, F flips the ray, Enter runs, 1 to 3 pick a tile. Each right round loads a crate on the dock, and the sixth reports game over (won) once, which completes the course step. Saves only which chapters are finished. English only.
